title: Enrich stat output with object references
objective: Add ref, objectType, and objectSchemaPath to sdlc stat output so recognized SDLC objects expose their canonical reference and persisted schema while ordinary files remain explicitly non-object.

branch.name: main
branch.rationale: The repository is already on the main branch and the user requested preparation and commit of the new work item on the current repository.

request.text: we need to add ref and objectType and objectSchemaPath to stat output. Prepare a new .docs/work-item and commit the work item

scope.name: stat-object-identity
scope.description: Add ref and objectType fields to the stat response for recognized SDLC work-item and task artifacts, with explicit null behavior for ordinary files.
scope.reason: Stat consumers need to distinguish a generic tracked file from a recognized SDLC object and identify that object canonically.

scope.name: stat-object-schema
scope.description: Add objectSchemaPath to identify the repository-relative persisted schema selected for a recognized object, with explicit null behavior when no object schema applies.
scope.reason: Consumers need to resolve the exact persisted object contract associated with stat output.

scope.name: stat-reference-coverage
scope.description: Cover representative generic files, work-item records, and task envelopes with focused and fresh-process stat tests.
scope.reason: The new fields cross object classification and reference conventions and must preserve existing stat behavior.

nonGoals.name: semantic-object-resolution
nonGoals.description: Do not resolve referenced entities, repositories, work items, tasks, or files beyond classifying the directly inspected repository path and constructing its canonical local reference.
nonGoals.reason: Stat remains a local read-only inspection command; semantic reference resolution belongs to other command boundaries.

nonGoals.name: stat-metadata-change
nonGoals.description: Do not change path containment, Git tracking checks, objectKind behavior, filesystem metadata fields, response schema identifier, or read-only semantics beyond adding the requested fields.
nonGoals.reason: WI-0008 enriches the existing response without changing its established inspection behavior.

nonGoals.name: provider-and-production-runtime
nonGoals.description: Do not add provider calls, HTTP services, persistence, deployment, or production release behavior.
nonGoals.reason: The work item is limited to local path classification and response serialization.

items.name: stat-object-fields
items.description: sdlc stat output must include ref, objectType, and objectSchemaPath fields in its persisted response contract.
items.reason: Consumers need a stable object identity and schema selection boundary in addition to filesystem metadata.

acceptanceCriteria.description: The sdlc/stat/v1 schema requires ref, objectType, and objectSchemaPath and remains closed.
Runtime stat output includes the three fields without removing or renaming existing response keys.

items.name: recognized-object-mapping
items.description: Stat must classify recognized work-item and task artifact paths with canonical local refs, object types, and repository-relative persisted schema paths.
items.reason: Recognized SDLC artifacts already have stable path conventions, reference grammars, and persisted schemas.

acceptanceCriteria.description: A tracked .docs/work-items/<id>/work-item.json response identifies the work-item object, uses a valid work-item-local ref, and selects schemas/work-item/v2/work-item.schema.json.

A tracked task envelope response identifies the task object, uses a valid work-item-local or task-qualified ref consistent with the inspected path, and selects schemas/sdlc-task-envelope/v1/sdlc-task-envelope.schema.json.

items.name: generic-file-boundary
items.description: Tracked files that are not recognized SDLC objects must remain valid stat responses with explicit null object-specific fields.
items.reason: README.md, package.json, and other ordinary files have no canonical SDLC object reference or object schema.

acceptanceCriteria.description: A tracked ordinary file response uses objectType file and has ref and objectSchemaPath set to null without changing existing path, tracking, or stat metadata.

items.name: stat-reference-tests
items.description: Focused tests must cover generic files, work-item objects, task objects, response schema validation, and read-only behavior through the public stat command.
items.reason: The response additions must remain stable across recognized and unrecognized tracked paths.

acceptanceCriteria.description: yarn test passes with representative generic, work-item, and task stat cases and the inspected files remain unchanged.
Representative successful stat responses validate against schemas/sdlc-stat/v1/sdlc-state.schema.json.
